claims.assertion: The driver cancelled on a passenger-no-show basis (chat F12: "Rider no-show, so I cancelled") and kept the $6.61 cancellation fee (F8), so the NS-1 conditions must all be met before the fee can stand.

NS-1(i) fails: the system timeline shows the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null, F7), and this system record defeats the driver's contrary statement in F12 and the chat message F10.

The one timeline entry that does show an "I'm Here" tap puts it at 17:18:50 (F6), and even on that record the driver pressed it 4 min 40 s after arrival — so the recorded tap time does not cure the conflict with F7; but if F6 is treated as the operative record, the rider was still not given the full 3 minutes from that tap before the 17:22:30 cancellation is considered, which the rider denies as a no-show at all.

NS-1(ii) fails on the GPS record: the driver was never at the pickup point when the fee logic required it — his closest approach was 34 m at 17:18:20 (F1) and he sat stationary 53 m from the pickup for the whole waiting period (F3), so the within-200 m requirement can only be satisfied in a de minimis sense over a period that began before any valid arrival indication.
Because at least one NS-1 condition is not fulfilled, NS-2 requires the full $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded to the rider rather than merely recorded.

The rider's own account in the complaint and the driver's chat are only statements; where the chat conflicts with the GPS/timeline records on whether the driver was actually at the pickup point and pressed "I'm Here", the system records govern.

The driver's account of having pressed "I'm Here" before waiting is contradicted by the record that the tap, if it occurred at all, came only at 17:18:50 (F6) while GPS already showed him inside 200 m from 17:17:50 (F2) and stationary from 17:18:25 (F3) — the arrival indication and the wait were not established as NS-1 requires.

The driver's cancellation was not caused by any road condition: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records exist on the route in the trip window (F13, F14), so nothing external excuses charging the rider.

The rider's profile supports treating this as a genuine, non-abusive complaint: 1354-day account, 4.4 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days (F16); the driver, by contrast, has 3 disputes with 2 upheld in 90 days including 2 no-show matters (F17), which warrants an account review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver's chat message at 17:19 (F10) and statement (F12) both assert he pressed "I'm Here", and the timeline fact F6 also shows a tap at 17:18:50 within 38 m of the pickup, which is well inside any plausible arrival radius — the other side will argue NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied on F6 alone.

F2 and F5 show the driver first within 200 m at 17:17:50 and still within 200 m for 4 min 40 s before cancelling at 17:22:30, and F6 says he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap — on those numbers NS-1(iii)'s >3 minutes of waiting is met, so the rider's best argument is about the pickup-radius and arrival-indication conflict (F1, F3, F7), not about wait duration.

The rider has no system record proving he arrived at the pickup point within the waiting period; his excuse ("came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is a statement only and there is no GPS/timeline fact for the rider's own position, so NS-4's logic that driver-not-yet-arrived is no defence cuts against him if NS-1 is found satisfied.

F7 (never tapped "I'm Here") and F6 (tapped at 17:18:50) come from the same timeline source and contradict each other; the judge may prefer F6 since it is the more specific record, which would collapse claim C2 and leave only the 34 m/53 m GPS distance points in F1 and F3 to argue on.

The driver's stationary period was only 53 m from the pickup (F3), which the other side will characterise as "at the pickup point" for the purposes of NS-1(ii) given Ryde does not publish an arrival radius (gap G2).

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 8 points
events.body:
→ D1: Proximity is not the test the driver needs: NS-1(ii) requires that the driver be at the pick-up point at the moment 'I'm Here' is pressed and throughout the wait, and the GPS record shows he was 34 m away at his closest (F1) and sat stationary 53 m from the pick-up for the entire waiting block (F3), never at the designated point. [F1 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2 (concedes): The $6.61 figure and the service type are not in dispute (F4, F8); what is in dispute is whether NS-1's conditions were ever satisfied, and NS-0/NS-1 make the fee payable only if they are. [F4 F8] [NS-0 NS-1]
→ D3: "Platform recorded arrival" is not the same as the driver pressing 'I'm Here' — NS-1(i) requires the tap, and the timeline records driver_pressed_here_at as null (F7); a waiting clock that starts without a valid arrival indication cannot satisfy NS-1(iii). [F7 F5 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: A 4 min 5 s stationary block at 53 m (F3) shows the driver held position short of the designated pick-up point; it does not show the rider was given the NS-1 conditions, and it is the same record the driver leans on for a proximity he was 19 m short of. [F3 F1] [NS-1]
→ D5: The 17:19 message (F10) is the driver's own assertion and is what the system record contradicts (F7); in-app notice from a driver who did not record a valid arrival cannot convert an unfulfilled NS-1 into a payable fee, and the 17:22 message (F11) was sent about half a minute before he cancelled at 17:22:30 (F4). [F10 F11 F7 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6 (concedes): Conceded as far as it goes — no weather or traffic factor is claimed by the rider either (F13, F14, F15) — but the absence of an exception neither creates an exception nor cures the missing NS-1(i)/(ii) elements (F7, F3). [F13 F14 F15 F7] [NS-1]
→ D7: The driver's history points the other way: 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show matters, in 90 days (F17), and the system record he invokes (F5) is the same source that records no 'I'm Here' tap (F7), so F5 cannot both be authoritative and selective. [F17 F5 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ C3: Withdrawn as flagged in the original brief; the rider's case stands on NS-1(i)/(ii) failing (F7, F1, F3) and NS-2 requiring the refund (F8). [F7 F1 F3 F8] [NS-2]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

The driver's account of having pressed "I'm Here" before waiting is contradicted by the record that the tap, if it occurred at all, came only at 17:18:50 (F6) while GPS already showed him inside 200 m from 17:17:50 (F2) and stationary from 17:18:25 (F3) — the arrival indication and the wait were not established as NS-1 requires.

The driver's cancellation was not caused by any road condition: no traffic incidents and no speed-band records exist on the route in the trip window (F13, F14), so nothing external excuses charging the rider.

The rider's profile supports treating this as a genuine, non-abusive complaint: 1354-day account, 4.4 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days (F16); the driver, by contrast, has 3 disputes with 2 upheld in 90 days including 2 no-show matters (F17), which warrants an account review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver's chat message at 17:19 (F10) and statement (F12) both assert he pressed "I'm Here", and the timeline fact F6 also shows a tap at 17:18:50 within 38 m of the pickup, which is well inside any plausible arrival radius — the other side will argue NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied on F6 alone.

F2 and F5 show the driver first within 200 m at 17:17:50 and still within 200 m for 4 min 40 s before cancelling at 17:22:30, and F6 says he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap — on those numbers NS-1(iii)'s >3 minutes of waiting is met, so the rider's best argument is about the pickup-radius and arrival-indication conflict (F1, F3, F7), not about wait duration.

The rider has no system record proving he arrived at the pickup point within the waiting period; his excuse ("came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is a statement only and there is no GPS/timeline fact for the rider's own position, so NS-4's logic that driver-not-yet-arrived is no defence cuts against him if NS-1 is found satisfied.

F7 (never tapped "I'm Here") and F6 (tapped at 17:18:50) come from the same timeline source and contradict each other; the judge may prefer F6 since it is the more specific record, which would collapse claim C2 and leave only the 34 m/53 m GPS distance points in F1 and F3 to argue on.

The driver's stationary period was only 53 m from the pickup (F3), which the other side will characterise as "at the pickup point" for the purposes of NS-1(ii) given Ryde does not publish an arrival radius (gap G2).

claims.assertion: The driver reached and remained at the pickup point: GPS shows his closest approach was 34 m and he was first within 200 m at 17:17:50, satisfying the 'at the pick-up location' element.
A ride-hailing cancellation fee is only payable on RydeX after the driver satisfies the arrival and waiting conditions; the fee on record is $6.61.
The waiting condition is met on the trip timeline: the platform recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and the driver waited within 200 m for 4 min 40 s before cancelling, exceeding the 3-minute threshold.
The driver's stationary period of 4 min 5 s at 53 m from the pickup point corroborates that he was holding at the pickup rather than abandoning it, and the rider never appeared.

The driver notified the rider in-app at 17:19 that he was at the pickup point and again at 17:22 that he had waited more than 3 minutes and was cancelling, so the rider was on notice before cancellation at 17:22:30.

No safety, traffic or reroute exception applies: no speed-band records or incidents were logged on the route in the trip window and weather was fair, so nothing displaces the ordinary no-show outcome.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes with 394 trips, and the rider's 'I came out a minute after the driver cancelled' account is contradicted by the system record that the driver waited 4 min 40 s after arrival, so the system record wins.

weaknesses: F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null, i.e. the timeline records that the driver never tapped 'I'm Here'; NS-1 (i) requires that tap, so the rider will argue the $6.61 must be refunded in full under NS-2, while F6 conflicts by recording a tap at 17:18:50.

The rider's complaint (a minute after cancellation) is supported by the fare fact that $6.61 was charged (F8) and by F17 showing the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which invites an abuse-of-cancellation-button flag against the driver.

The flat 4 min 5 s stationary block at 53 m (F3) can be read by the rider as the driver idling short of the door rather than at the designated pickup point, weakening the 'at the pick-up location' element.

points.response: Proximity is not the test the driver needs: NS-1(ii) requires that the driver be at the pick-up point at the moment 'I'm Here' is pressed and throughout the wait, and the GPS record shows he was 34 m away at his closest (F1) and sat stationary 53 m from the pick-up for the entire waiting block (F3), never at the designated point.
The $6.61 figure and the service type are not in dispute (F4, F8); what is in dispute is whether NS-1's conditions were ever satisfied, and NS-0/NS-1 make the fee payable only if they are.

"Platform recorded arrival" is not the same as the driver pressing 'I'm Here' — NS-1(i) requires the tap, and the timeline records driver_pressed_here_at as null (F7); a waiting clock that starts without a valid arrival indication cannot satisfy NS-1(iii).

A 4 min 5 s stationary block at 53 m (F3) shows the driver held position short of the designated pick-up point; it does not show the rider was given the NS-1 conditions, and it is the same record the driver leans on for a proximity he was 19 m short of.

The 17:19 message (F10) is the driver's own assertion and is what the system record contradicts (F7); in-app notice from a driver who did not record a valid arrival cannot convert an unfulfilled NS-1 into a payable fee, and the 17:22 message (F11) was sent about half a minute before he cancelled at 17:22:30 (F4).

Conceded as far as it goes — no weather or traffic factor is claimed by the rider either (F13, F14, F15) — but the absence of an exception neither creates an exception nor cures the missing NS-1(i)/(ii) elements (F7, F3).

The driver's history points the other way: 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show matters, in 90 days (F17), and the system record he invokes (F5) is the same source that records no 'I'm Here' tap (F7), so F5 cannot both be authoritative and selective.
Withdrawn as flagged in the original brief; the rider's case stands on NS-1(i)/(ii) failing (F7, F1, F3) and NS-2 requiring the refund (F8).

Conceded as to the framework: the driver cancelled citing rider no-show and the $6.61 fee stands only if all NS-1 elements are met — my case is that they are met, but I do not dispute that NS-0/NS-1 is the sole gateway.

F7 (null tap) and F6 (tap recorded at 17:18:50, 38 m from the pickup) come from the same timeline source and conflict; the more specific record F6 shows the arrival indication was pressed, and F10's chat message and F12's statement align with F6 rather than contradicting it, so NS-1(i) is satisfied on the specific record.

Even on the 17:18:50 tap the waiting element is met: the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap (F6) and cancelled at 17:22:30 (F4), i.e. more than 3:01 of waiting counted from the tap, so NS-1(iii) holds regardless of which arrival timestamp is used.

NS-1(ii) is met on the GPS record: the driver was first within 200 m at 17:17:50 and was inside that range for 4 min 40 s before cancelling (F2), his closest approach was 34 m (F1), and a 53 m stationary hold (F3) is plainly 'at the pick-up location' given Ryde publishes no arrival radius.

NS-2 does not trigger because no NS-1 element fails: (i) satisfied per F6, (ii) satisfied per F2/F1 (34 m closest approach, within 200 m for 4 min 40 s), and (iii) satisfied per F6 (3 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap), so no refund arises.

The system records here favour the driver, not the rider: F2, F5 and F6 record arrival within 200 m and more than three minutes of waiting, and the rider's 'came out a minute after' account has no GPS or timeline fact behind it, so the system record defeats the rider's statement alone.

The sequence the rider calls contradictory is exactly compliant: the driver entered 200 m at 17:17:50 (F2), held stationary from 17:18:25 (F3), and the recorded tap at 17:18:50 (F6) was followed by 3 min 40 s still inside 200 m before the 17:22:30 cancellation (F4), so the arrival indication and the wait both preceded the cancellation.

Traffic is irrelevant to this no-show claim: with no incidents and no speed-band records in the trip window (F13, F14) and fair weather (F15), NS-3 is not engaged because the driver cancelled on a passenger-no-show basis that satisfies NS-1, not for want of a valid reason.

The rider's profile (F16) cannot create a refund and the driver's profile (F17) cannot decide it — profile facts may only support an additional action — and NS-2's flag is triggered only when the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while GPS placed him outside the pickup range, which F1/F2 refute (34 m, within 200 m for 4 min 40 s); I also note the two upheld no-show matters on the driver's 90-day record are outweighed by the system record here.

notices.text: We looked into your dispute of the $6.61 no-show fee on your RydeX trip. The fee stands and no voucher is being issued. Two facts decided this: the driver's phone registered arrival at the pickup at 5:18pm, and the driver stayed within a couple of hundred metres of the pickup for more than three minutes before cancelling. Chats at 5:19pm and 5:22pm, plus the GPS trail, matched that. Nothing changes on your account. We did flag the arrival-tap logging for a data check, but that does not affect the outcome for you.

Your $6.61 rider no-show cancellation fee stands, and it will be applied to your account as normal. We confirmed you arrived at the pickup and waited more than three minutes before cancelling, based on the arrival record at 5:18pm and the location trail showing you close to the pickup for over four minutes. No account action is being taken against you. One tip for next time: send your waiting messages earlier in the wait window — the 5:19pm and 5:22pm chats came late. You will keep receiving no-show fees on the same basis.
